blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction builds 3D scenes directly from input images for novel view rendering, but learning Gaussian attributes from predicted geometry for high-quality rendering under large viewpoint changes remains challenging. We analyze limitations in Gaussian attribute learning and introduce InfiniSplat v2, which improves rendering quality through architectural and training changes. Our method decouples geometry and attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch, aligns predicted Gaussians using ground-truth camera poses during training, and adopts large-angle target view supervision. Across six datasets, the feed-forward outputs of the same trained model achieve state-of-the-art mean LPIPS and DISTS among the evaluated methods in both pose-conditioned and pose-free settings. In the pose-conditioned setting, mean LPIPS and DISTS decrease by 25.8% and 32.9%, respectively, compared with the strongest evaluated baselines. We further find that opacity learned with only image reconstruction supervision suppresses geometrically inconsistent points. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat2/

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Image-based 3D scene reconstruction aims to recover a renderable 3D scene
from input images to support novel view rendering for applications such as
simulation, content creation, and autonomous driving. 3D Gaussian Splatting
(3DGS) ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) enables efficient rendering through an explicit scene
representation. Building on this representation, recent feed-forward
methods ( Charatan et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2024a ; Zhang et al., 2024 ; Xu et al., 2025b ) directly predict Gaussian
scenes from input images, eliminating the need for per-scene representation
optimization at inference time.

blocks.en: As shown in Fig. 1 , InfiniSplat v2 reconstructs Gaussian scenes from predicted multi-view geometry and supports high-quality novel-view rendering at extreme viewpoints. We identify key factors that affect Gaussian learning and introduce three corresponding architectural and training improvements. First, we investigate why prior methods struggle to eliminate flying-point artifacts and find that jointly optimizing geometry and Gaussian attributes leads to geometric degradation. We therefore redesign the architecture to decouple geometry prediction from Gaussian attribute prediction while keeping the geometry branch frozen. Second, we find that using predicted camera poses during training ( Lin et al., 2025 ) introduces pose errors. Under large-angle supervision, these errors can misguide the network during training. We therefore use GT camera poses to align the predicted Gaussians. Third, inspired by InfiniSplat’s strong performance under large viewpoint changes ( Wang et al., 2026b ) , we introduce large-angle target view supervision for feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction from arbitrary input views. Our experiments show that these three improvements enhance novel view rendering quality under large viewpoint changes, even when the predicted point clouds contain numerous outliers.

blocks.en: 2.2 Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting

blocks.en:
Generalizable view synthesis learns to predict novel views or renderable
representations across scenes ( Wang et al., 2021 ; Hong et al., 2024 ; Jin et al., 2024 ) . Feed-forward Gaussian
methods pursue this goal by directly predicting explicit Gaussian scenes.
SHARP ( Mescheder et al., 2026 ) and InfiniSplat ( Wang et al., 2026b ) reconstruct scenes
from a single image, while GS-LRM ( Zhang et al., 2024 ) combines multiple views.
NoPoSplat ( Ye et al., 2025 ) and FLARE ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) support reconstruction without supplied camera poses. Long-LRM ( Ziwen et al., 2025 ) and tttLRM ( Wang et al., 2026a ) further extend reconstruction to long input sequences.
Work on Gaussian representations also explores different ways to organize
and predict primitives: C3G ( An et al., 2025 ) and TokenGS ( Ren et al., 2026 ) use learnable
queries or tokens, while VolSplat ( Wang et al., 2025b ) predicts voxel-aligned
Gaussians.

More directly related to our work is how geometry is estimated and used
for Gaussian prediction. pixelSplat ( Charatan et al., 2024 ) establishes cross-view
correspondences through epipolar attention, while MVSplat ( Chen et al., 2024a ) estimates depth using multi-view cost volumes. DepthSplat ( Xu et al., 2025b ) augments multi-view depth estimation with pretrained monocular depth features.
Learned geometric priors also support Gaussian prediction in
AnySplat ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) , WorldMirror ( Liu et al., 2025 ; Team et al., 2026 ) ,
and DA3-GS ( Lin et al., 2025 ) .
Building on such priors,
SplatAnything ( Anonymous, 2027 ) scales up training with diverse synthetic
and real-world data. QuerySplat ( Li et al., 2026 ) separately decodes
geometry and appearance from frozen geometric features.
Our work focuses on learning Gaussian attributes from imperfect predicted
point clouds to support high-quality novel view rendering.

branch adapts to rendering
through image reconstruction supervision

using input-view rendering feedback.

blocks.en:
Our goal is to improve Gaussian attributes through image reconstruction
supervision without compensating for attribute errors by moving point
positions. We therefore freeze the geometry branch and keep Gaussian centers
fixed at the back-projected point positions.
Constructing points with predicted input poses while supervising
them from GT target poses can also introduce camera-induced residuals;
we use scale-aligned GT cameras for both operations during training.
Finally, targets near the input viewing directions may leave Gaussian shape
insufficiently constrained. We favor large-angle target views to constrain
scales and orientations through projections from different directions.
Figure 2 illustrates the resulting training pipeline.

blocks.en:
InfiniSplat v2 improves mean LPIPS and DISTS across six datasets in both
pose settings. ETH3D and DTU ablations support fixed centers and attribute
adaptation under reconstruction supervision. Learned opacity preferentially
suppresses geometrically inconsistent points.

blocks.en: A.6 Camera Protocol and Evaluation Metrics

blocks.en:
Pose-conditioned and pose-free results are reported and ranked separately.
In the pose-free setting, reference input cameras are not reconstruction
inputs; they only establish the evaluation reference frame and estimate
translation scale from input-camera correspondences. The scene is constructed
before evaluation-camera alignment and remains unchanged. Target poses define
rendering queries without entering the fit. Alignment rescales reference-relative
translations only, rather than applying a full Sim(3) transform.
For methods predicting intrinsics, target focal lengths are the component-wise
median of predicted input focal lengths, scaled to the target resolution,
with the reference principal point retained. In the pose-conditioned setting,
reference input cameras are available for reconstruction and target intrinsics
are fixed to GT. Evaluation target RGB is never used for reconstruction or refinement feedback.

blocks.en: Appendix C Limitations and Future Work
blocks.zh: 附录C 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en:
Opacity learning and pruning can suppress unreliable Gaussians, but fixed
centers cannot correct severe errors in predicted geometry. Reconstruction
quality therefore remains limited by the geometric prior. Pixel-aligned
prediction also produces redundancy not fully removed by voxel merging,
while limited input coverage can leave holes in unobserved regions.
Future work will explore stronger geometric priors and more compact Gaussian
representations, as well as generative models and camera-trajectory design
to address limited coverage.
blocks.zh:
不透明度的学习和修行可以抑制不可靠的高斯人,但固定
中心无法校正预测几何中的严重错误 。 重建
因此,质量仍受前几何的限制。 像素对齐
预测还会产生不完全被阴道合并去除的冗余,
虽然投入覆盖面有限,但可能会给未观测地区留下漏洞。
今后的工作将探讨更强几何前科和更紧凑的高斯人
说明,以及基因模型和相机-外射设计
处理有限的覆盖面。
